science.title: FOXO3 induces chromatin changes in a model of DNA damage-induced senescence
science.description: FOXO transcription factors are critical for cellular homeostasis and the stress response and have been implicated in longevity in several species. Yet, how these factors function at the chromatin level in differing conditions in human cells is poorly understood. Here, we take an integrated multi-omics approach to identify the chromatin-level mechanisms by which FOXO3 coordinates transcriptional programs in replicating cells and in a model of cellular senescence. In a DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 levels are elevated early in senescence entry. Increased FOXO3 expression induces expression of chromatin remodeling factors, and impacts chromatin accessibility across the genome together with SWI/SNF chromatin remodelers. As cells enter DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 is essential for chromatin remodeling and reprogramming of a genomic network that functions to modulate cell stress and lineage-specific cellular functions. Altogether, we identify a FOXO3-SWI/SNF network that regulates key cellular processes including metabolism, proteostasis, epigenetics, and cell lineage, and is dynamically controlled under DNA damaging conditions.

science.title: Brown adipose tissue ankyrin-B cell-autonomously modulates lipid content and its deletion protects male mice against diet-induced obesity
science.description: Fatty acid (FA) availability for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis depends in part on lipolysis of lipid droplet (LD) triglycerides. Here, we identify the membrane adaptor ankyrin-B (AnkB), encoded by the cardiometabolic disease-associated ANK2 gene, as a regulator of brown adipocyte lipid homeostasis and metabolic adaptation. BAT-specific AnkB deficiency caused excess lipid accumulation, enlarged LDs, and BAT whitening without altering mitochondrial oxidative capacity or thermogenesis in the fed state in male mice. Mechanistically, AnkB promoted basal lipolysis by recruiting hormone-sensitive lipase to LDs. However, AnkB loss compromised thermoregulation during cold exposure with fasting, linking AnkB-dependent FA release to thermogenesis under energetic stress. Unexpectedly, BAT AnkB deficiency protected male mice from high-fat diet-induced obesity (DIO), hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, and insulin resistance. This protection was associated with enhanced BAT mitochondrial oxidative capacity, oxidative remodeling of white adipose tissue, and increased circulating FGF21. Together, these findings establish AnkB as a previously unrecognized regulator of BAT lipid mobilization that coordinates thermogenic fuel availability with mitochondrial oxidative adaptation during metabolic stress. Ankyrin-B couples BAT lipid droplet lipolysis to thermogenic fuel availability. Its loss impairs thermoregulation during fasting but preserves fed-state thermogenesis and protects against diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

science.title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California
science.description: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation. Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability.
